issue.title: Support GraalVM / native image builds using the GraalVM Java 11 build
issue.body:
**Description**
A follow up to #4218 which did the upgrade to GraalVM version 19.3 but focused only on the "JDK8 flavoured edition"

body: I didn't spend much time on this one yesterday and I won't be able to work on it before tonight, so feel free to take it over if you're able to submit a PR today.

This one is caused by `HystrixInitializer` which is an `@ApplicationScoped` bean eagerly initialized at application startup. When it is constructed, it injects a `DefaultHystrixConcurrencyStrategy` instance which itself calls `Executors.privilegedThreadFactory()` during its own construction. This last call is forbidden during the native image build time as it initializes the `FilePermission` class.

@mkouba: Would have an idea of a reasonnable way to delay the `HystrixInitializer` initialization? (I tried a few silly things but I'm pretty sure there's a simple solution here)

Hm, the `HystrixInitializer` declares an `@Observes @Initialized(ApplicationScoped.class) Object` observer and there is currently no easy way to ignore/change this observer. I think that we'll need to add an `ObserverTransformer` build-time extension so that it would be possible to transform the observer. But the problem is the event type. So in this particular case, we would need a replacement for `javax.enterprise.inject.spi.ProcessObserverMethod.veto()` AND initialize the `HystrixInitializer` in an `@Observes StartupEvent` observer. @manovotn WDYT?
Oh then I wasn’t that silly :) Combining StartupEvent and a veto on the bean is exactly what I tried to do but I couldn’t find a way to make it work. Thanks for your quick answer!

> BTW, I tried to fix the issue in a different way with a substitution but it didn't work.

I'm not sure. What error do you get?

> Should I substitute the code of a generated bean somehow?

No, the generated bean does not contain the logic. It's more like a metadata holder.

> I'm not sure. What error do you get?

Absolutely no error. I will add more debug logging.

> No, the generated bean does not contain the logic. It's more like a metadata holder.

That was my understanding too.

>  I think that we'll need to add an ObserverTransformer build-time extension so that it would be possible to transform the observer. But the problem is the event type. 

Hmm, last time I mentioned observer transformation for this specific event, @mkouba was against ;-)
For this specific case, shouldn't we instead look into making the the init in smallrye extensible, so that in Quarkus there is a bean that listens to `StartupEvent` instead and performs the init? I feel like the transformation is kind of an overkill here. Or, we could remove the observer and perform eager init in some other way, for instance calling a dummy method on that bean from somewhere when we know its initialized - In Quarkus this is the `StartupEvent`, for standalone SR, this can be done via an observer on a different bean that we veto. Something along those lines?

> So in this particular case, we would need a replacement for javax.enterprise.inject.spi.ProcessObserverMethod.veto() AND initialize the HystrixInitializer in an @Observes StartupEvent observer.

If we don't do transformers (and want to fix this purely in quarkus code), then yes, we need a way to veto observers and then add a custom one. Ideally, we don't even want to create metadata for vetoed OM which is where it would get tangled a bit...

> Hmm, last time I mentioned observer transformation for this specific event, @mkouba was against ;-)

That's possible. I often change my mind when I see a real use case ;-).

> For this specific case, shouldn't we instead look into making the the init in smallrye extensible

+1. On the other hand, this looks like a common pattern.

> Or, we could remove the observer and perform...

You mean in SM, right? The problem is that we don't always control the codebase.

> Ideally, we don't even want to create metadata for vetoed OM which is where it would get tangled a bit...

My initial idea was to create an `ObserverTransformer` that can:
1) modify the observed type,
2) modify the set of qualifiers,
3) veto the observer.

> modify the observed type,

For general use case, this is very dangerous. Imagine you observe any non-Object type. Your code can attempt to do anything with it and now we would allow people to change that type which will blow up of course. I know CDI extensions allow to break a lot of things already, but this just smells fishy...

The other two capabilities are fine by me.

> You mean in SM, right? The problem is that we don't always control the codebase.

Yes, I meant in SM codebase. I know we don't always control it, yet here we do and to me, this doesn't seem as that common problem, but maybe I am just missing some other reports/issues on this?

> The other two capabilities are fine by me.

You're right. It would be safer not to support that kind of stuff!
